name: Distance-preserving decomposition of an odd spider
summary: A (2n+1)-legged Z-spider is fault-equivalent to an n- and an (n+1)-legged spider joined through n four-legged spiders.
description: A phase-free Z-spider with $2n+1$ legs can be decomposed into an $n$-legged spider, an $(n+1)$-legged spider and $n$ four-legged spiders: each four-legged spider carries two of the original legs and is connected to both other spiders, and the remaining leg is on the $(n+1)$-legged spider. The rewrite is distance-preserving (equivalently, fault-equivalent under edge-flip noise). The proof considers the null space of the detector error matrix of the right-hand side over $\mathbb F_2$ and shows that every undetectable combination of flips can be pushed to the boundary without increasing its weight.

source.location: Sec. 3.3, rewrite $(r_{2n^+})$; proof in the appendix

parameter_notes: A spider with 2n + 1 legs, built from an n-legged spider, an (n + 1)-legged spider and n four-legged spiders (shown for n = 2); holds for any n ≥ 1.
